overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the notice was defective for a planned hearing, but because no hearing was held the Committee did not discuss the matter improperly, and the chair's limit on public participation was within his discretion.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 2, 2016 notice failed to say the Committee would hold a public hearing on a particular certification matter.
allegations.key_passage: Because it did not hold a hearing, however, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing a matter of which sufficient notice had not been given.

allegations.summary: Review of whether the chair limited public participation at the March 2, 2016 meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: It is within the Chair's discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, and thus he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by doing so here.

allegations.summary: Implicit complaint that the Committee improperly held or failed to hold a hearing under separate hearing and notice laws (780 CMR 110.R7, 801 CMR 1.02).
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether there was a violation of any separate law that may have required a hearing.
